examples.knowledge_point: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base
examples.worked_solution:
Here, we apply our formula for the derivative when the base of the logarithm is a number other than $e.$ By doing so, we obtain

$$
\eqalign{
			\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}&=\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(4\log_3 x\right)\
									 &=4\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\log_3 x\right)\
									 &=4\cdot\dfrac{1}{x \ln 3}\
									&=\dfrac{4}{x \ln 3}.

}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given the function  $y=4ln⁡x-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}+5$, find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4ln⁡x-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}+5) \\  & =\frac{4}{x}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}ln⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=2} & ={(\frac{4}{x}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{x}ln⁡(2))|}_{x=2} \\  & =\frac{4}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {2}^{2}ln⁡(2) \\  & =2-\frac{4}{3}ln⁡(2)\,.\end{aligned}
$$
